Columns read: County, Last Name, First Name, Middle Name, Suffix, Party, Office, Office Description, District, Unexpired, Withdrawn, Disqualified, Deceased. Of 6,794 rows, 297 are marked withdrawn (271), disqualified (7) or deceased (19) and left off; the page's own directory counts the other 6,497 office by office, and every office's count matched. 6,290 rows are placed, each in one contest; 207 name no city, school district or district that can be told: 5 of them are found by name on a county clerk's official ballot (that source's note says how), and the other 202 are listed as gaps, county by county. Of the rows placed, 35 repeat a candidate already in the contest (a city or school district that two county clerks list, or one name twice) and count once; 0 are left off because the other county clerk's list marks the same candidate withdrawn; and 108 belong to the 35 contests where the list still shows more than one candidate of a party for one seat, which are kept without names. That leaves 6,147 candidates. 0 contests are kept with no name because everyone who filed for them is marked withdrawn, disqualified or deceased. Where a county clerk's official ballots were read, they settle the contests they print, and the counts above are before that (see that source). The list holds each name in four columns, the family name in capitals; names are shown here in ordinary capitals, given names first, with Jr, Sr, II, III or IV after the family name. A courtesy title in the Suffix column (31 rows) is left out; a nickname there (19 rows) is kept after the given names. The list gives no ballot order. Cities and school districts are named only in the free-text Office Description column, and a row is tied to one only when that text fits exactly one name on the Census Bureau's lists: 2,941 rows by the name as printed, 29 by part of a name, 15 by a name one slip of spelling away, 215 because the county has one city, and 373 school board rows by the division number of the county's own school district. 22 rows filed under City Legislative Body whose description says Mayor are shown as candidates for mayor. 25 rows for school board and soil and water offices carry a party in the list; those offices are nonpartisan and no party is shown. A district number on a county-wide office (23 rows) is ignored, and where the District column and the description give different numbers (3 rows) the column is used. 1 kept cell held contact details a clerk had typed into it: it is blanked before anything is kept, and its row is listed with the gaps.

ky-sbe-election-schedule-2026-2036.note: Which offices are elected in which year. Checked in its marks: county officers are elected in 2026; district judges are elected in 2026; part of each school board is elected in 2026; mayors are elected in 2026 and 2028, by turns; city legislative bodies are elected every even year; circuit court clerks are next elected in 2030; circuit judges are next elected in 2030; Commonwealth's attorneys are next elected in 2030; statewide officers are elected in 2027.

local_calendar.t: On November 3, 2026 Kentucky elects each county's officers (judge/executive, magistrates or commissioners, county clerk, county attorney, sheriff, jailer, coroner, surveyor, property valuation administrator and constables), its district judges, every city council and commission, the mayors and school board members whose four-year terms are ending, and soil and water conservation district supervisors. Statewide officers are elected in 2027, and circuit judges, circuit court clerks and Commonwealth's attorneys in 2030, so the few such seats on this ballot are filled only for the time left until then. The other mayors and school board seats, and Louisville's even-numbered Metro Council districts, are elected in 2028.
